caption: sky note: "saturday's eclipse turns the moon blood red." not true. feb 20 is a penumbral eclipse in virgo (23:12 utc): faint, not red.

slides.headline: “the feb 20 eclipse turns the moon blood red”
slides.body: that red picture is a total lunar eclipse. feb 20 is penumbral: the moon only skims earth's pale outer shadow. it stays its normal colour, maybe a touch dimmer on one edge.

slides.headline: red needs the dark *core* of earth's shadow
slides.body: the moon turns copper only inside the umbra, lit by sunlight bent through our atmosphere. this time it misses the umbra entirely.

slides.headline: a quiet eclipse still reads as an *ending*
slides.body: astrologers read eclipses as fast-forwards, faint or not. nothing about this one changes everything. it might change one habit, if you let it.

slides.headline: no blood moon. still a good night to say the *honest* thing.
slides.body: send this to whoever posted the red one.
